dispositions.selection_rule: The thin-year rule (register Y-THIN, chosen by the owner on 23 November 2026 and amended the same night with the owner's choice B1): an item, counted by its own words, is eligible when it was printed by more than half of the newspapers that survive for its weeks, and by at least 4; the eligible items printed by every newspaper that survives for their weeks are admitted (27 in 1794), and the others are chosen to cover the months and the kinds of news, about as many stories as a standard year (a target, not a quota); one affair's items are handled as in X-1800-01; the eligible items not chosen are listed here.
dispositions.paper_counting: 1794 has 9 catalogue series, which are 8 papers (C-04): the Gazette of the United States under two catalogue numbers (sn83025878 to 11 June, sn84026271 from 12 June). The Eagle of Hanover (3 issues) and the Phoenix of Dover (1 issue) survive only in a few weeks, and the Columbian Informer of Keene from February; 4 to 7 papers are in print in any three weeks, so an item needs 4 papers all year.

dispositions.method: The automatic families first printed in 1794 that reach 3 or more papers, long-running ones included, were split into single printed items (story_items.py --long-running, items.json: 1,022 items, 383 in 4 or more catalogue series by the finder's count), and the families of 1793 were looked for on the 1794 pages (items_from_1793.json: 78 items). Every item in 3 or more papers was counted by machine by about 100 words of its text from the finder's position, over all 2,119 pages in both transcriptions (a dense run of its word 5-grams, at least a quarter of them); the counts were joined into documents only where two items stand at the same place on the same pages, because the papers print runs of short foreign paragraphs. Every item the machine put in every surviving paper, and the news considered for choosing, was counted again by about 70 words from its own opening (counts_1794.json), and the pages that print another text sharing the words (the London Gazette's formula for its dispatches, the forms of the King's instructions) were read and left out. Each admitted printing was checked against its page scan.

counted_item_by_item.Paper counts: Counted by their own words, 366 items of 1794 are eligible: 247 in 4 papers, 102 in 5, 16 in 6, 1 in 7. 27 items are printed by every paper that survives for their weeks and are admitted; 8 more are chosen to cover the months and the kinds of news (one affair's three items under a parent story). 10 more eligible items counted by their opening are not chosen, and 321 documents of the item finder are eligible by their own words and not chosen; all are listed with their counts. 6 candidates counted by their opening are below the bar and listed. 427 more documents of the item finder are in 3 papers or fewer by their own words, below the bar (docs_1794.json); they are not listed one by one.
counted_item_by_item.Titles of the items not chosen: Each eligible document of the item finder not chosen is listed by its own words: the dateline or heading before the finder's position and the words that follow (some begin inside the item, where the finder's position does); a notice or advertisement that names a private person is described instead (R-04). Each candidate counted by its opening is listed by a title of the review's.
